item.title: A 50-year-old theory about evolution may have been wrong all along
item.description: A decades-old theory suggesting that evolution protects its most important genes from mutations has been dealt a major blow. An extensive new analysis of mutations in bacteria and yeast found no evidence that essential genes mutate less frequently than other genes. Researchers say earlier studies may have been misled by harmful mutations that disappeared through natural selection before scientists could detect them. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: An ancient failed rift is reawakening inside one of Africa's oldest landmasses
item.description: In April 2017, a magnitude 6.5 earthquake shook southern Africa from an unlikely place: the middle of the Kalahari Craton in eastern Botswana. Cratons are the ancient cores of continents, and this one is built from blocks of crust up to 3.7 billion years old. Geologists have long considered such regions too cold, too thick and too rigid to tear apart. Fuente: Phys.org.

The show’s emotional power is distilled in a viral scene when two women who barely spoke to each other for seven years sit across a small wooden table. item.title: Scientists say the human family tree may need a radical rewrite
item.description: The human family tree may need a major overhaul. New research from Monash University challenges the traditional classification of our ancient ancestors, arguing that species such as Australopithecus and Paranthropus should be grouped within our own genus, Homo. As scientists uncover more fossils and analyze evolutionary relationships, the boundaries that once separated these ancient relatives are becoming increasingly difficult to defend.
